newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian party faction urged to reopen HQ.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian party faction urged to reopen HQ.

text.p: Indonesia has urged leaders of a government-backed faction of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) to reopen its head office, which has been closed since a police raid five weeks ago, a newspaper said on Tuesday.

The Jakarta Post quoted Interior Minister Yogie Memet as saying the building must be quickly re-opened after being damaged in the July 27 raid during which loyalist supporters of former PDI leader Megawati Sukarnoputri were ejected.
"The new board must take up office at the secretariat as soon as possible," Memet said.
The building has remained unoccupied and under police guard since the raid.
"Fixing the building may cost money. There may have to be an invocation, there could be a lot of ghosts in that office," Memet said.
The building was occupied by Megawati supporters after a government-funded congress in Medan, North Sumatra in June elected deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi as party leader.
Megawati, daughter of late founding President Sukarno, said the congress was unconstitutional and illegal as she had been elected PDI leader for a five year term in 1993.
Hundreds of police retook the headquarters from Megawati loyalists on July 27 after it was earlier attacked by Surjadi supporters.
The attack sparked the worst riots in the capital for over 20 years in which at least five people died.
PDI executive members loyal to Megawati have said since that as they are the legal leaders of the PDI they will open a new office to conduct their affairs.

"It is difficult to always have meetings at Megawati's home and so we are looking for an office and when we find it we will declare it openly," senior party member and Megawati loyalist Kwik Gian Gie told Reuters recently.
